title: Triage rubric for egress-restricted & maintenance-window private deployments
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We receive a steady stream of private/VPC/on-prem requests that appear similar but have subtly different network constraints: (A) customers that prohibit outbound egress except to a pinned proxy, (B) customers that allow intermittent egress during scheduled maintenance windows, and (C) fully air-gapped customers with zero egress. Current intake forms and scoring produce false positives for feasibility and lead to long discovery cycles.

Objective: Deliver a compact triage rubric and intake flows that quickly classify requests into: self-serve (low effort), engineering-assisted with connector/proxy patterns (medium effort), or platform-engaged multi-week projects (high effort). The rubric should prioritize by customer risk, revenue signal, upgrade/patchability, and security/regulatory constraints.

Scope: Non-bug customer requests only — onboarding, upgrade scheduling, networking readiness, and air-gap exceptions. Excludes runway billing/legal and post-deployment incidents. This ticket will: 1) define the rubric and scoring thresholds, 2) map default remediation lanes and playbooks for each lane, 3) draft updated intake questions and CLI probe checklist for solutions engineers, 4) produce a short runbook snippet for the sales concierge to set expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Compact rubric (<= 10 checks) that classifies requests into Low/Medium/High delivery effort with example signals
Updated intake form JSON for self-serve gating and an explanatory help text for each question
Playbook mapping: for each classification, a clear set of next steps (tech approach, owner, ETA), including fallbacks
Sample communications templates for Sales/SE to set rollout/upgrade expectations
Two pilot customers (one egress-limited, one scheduled-window) validated the rubric and provided feedback
updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — aligned PM/SE/Eng on problem statement. Identified recurring blocker: customers with 'egress-only-to-corporate-proxy' need a lightweight proxy pattern docs.

2026-03-11: Fast research — reviewed 18 intake requests from last 9 months. 45% were egress-constrained, 30% were scheduled-window-only, 25% air-gapped. Revenue signal for these requests skewed high (avg ACV > $120k).

2026-03-12: Workshop with Solutions Eng and Security (1 hour). Trade-offs discussed: recommend 'hosted proxy bridge' pattern vs 'bastion-triggered agent'. Decided to pilot proxy bridge for mid-effort lane due to lower ops burden.

2026-03-12: Drafted initial rubric with 9 checks: egress availability, pinned IPs allowed, customer willingness for scheduled windows, KMS/HSM integration requirement, cert rotation path, upgrade cadence tolerance, patch rollback policy, observability/shipping constraints, legal/data residency notes.

2026-03-13: Design reviewed playbook for scheduled-window installs (SE-run, 2-4 week timeline). Added requirement: customer signs maintenance SLA allowing 2x 4-hour windows/month for upgrades. SE requested a preflight network probe script — created stub and filed ENG-21107 for automation.

2026-03-14: Security review sync: confirmed proxy bridge design requires egress to a pinned FQDN and mTLS. Security requested a short downscoped threat model and rotation guidance — added as deliverable. Updated ticket scope to include short security checklist.
decisions: Adopt three-tier delivery lanes: Self-serve (low), Proxy-bridge (medium), Onsite/Agent (high).
Proxy-bridge wins pilot over bastion/agent because it reduces customer maintenance and our ops footprint; agent approach remains for fully air-gapped/high-security customers but is high effort.
Scoring threshold: 0-2 checks fail -> Self-serve; 3-5 checks fail -> Proxy-bridge lane; 6+ checks fail -> High-effort (operator-engaged).
Require minimal legal sign-off only for medium lane; require SOC/compliance intake for high lane.
